candidates.exact_span: If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable receiving water test met the following stipulations:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of 'unsatisfactory,' 'instream toxicity,' or 'test acceptance criteria,' and whether substitution is permitted, change which toxicity-test methodology applies, whether resulting measurements are usable for numeric limit comparison, and whether adequate evidence exists for tests conducted after a failed receiving-water control.

candidates.exact_span: a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance requirements was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this concurrent-control condition is met determines if synthetic dilution water may be used in later tests, affecting applicable monitoring methodology (B) and whether subsequent test evidence is adequately documented or must be treated as missing/invalid (C).

candidates.exact_span: the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to completion,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'carried out to completion' affects whether the permittee satisfied procedural monitoring obligations tied to substitution (B) and whether partial or incomplete tests count as established evidence versus unresolved missing-evidence states (C).

candidates.exact_span: the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity with the full report and information required; and
candidates.computation_change_reason: What must be included in the 'full report and information required' governs reporting/monitoring obligations after a toxic receiving-water result (B) and whether toxicity-related evidence is documented or remains an unresolved no-data case (C).

candidates.exact_span: the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How 'similar' is judged, which reference water applies, and whether parameter magnitudes 'cause toxicity' affect validity of substituted dilution-water tests used for compliance comparison (A), applicable test-design monitoring requirements (B), and whether test results constitute adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a minimum of three samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the minimum sample count and when a flow-weighted composite is required versus optional changes whether baseline toxicity sampling obligations were applicable and satisfied (B) and whether available sample evidence is adequate (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second and third sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when second and third samples/composites are required for dilution renewals affects applicable monitoring frequency and timing obligations (B) and whether missing samples reflect conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample. The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample. Samples shall be chilled to 6 degrees Centigrade during collection, shipping, and/or storage. A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of holding-time limits, initiation deadlines, chilling requirements, and whether EPA/NMED notification extends holding to 72 hours affect whether samples/tests meet permit conditions, which in turn changes limit-comparison validity (A), monitoring compliance obligations (B), and whether results are established evidence or unresolved due to procedural deficiency (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How 'representative of the discharge duration' and coverage of chlorination, biocide, or intermittent toxic episodes are interpreted changes when sampling is required and whether absent or mistimed samples indicate conditional non-requirement or missing required evidence (C), affecting monitoring-obligation applicability (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall prepare a full report of the results of all tests conducted pursuant to this part in accordance with the Report Preparation Section of the most current publication of the method manual, for every valid or invalid toxicity test initiated, whether carried to completion or not. The permittee shall retain each full report and submit them upon the specific request of the Agency.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scope of 'full report,' reference to the 'most current publication of the method manual,' and inclusion of valid, invalid, completed, and incomplete initiated tests define reporting/monitoring documentation obligations (B) and how missing or partial records are classified among documented no-data, conditional non-requirement, or inadequate-evidence states (C).
